title: ChatGPT Is Still Not Good Enough at Giving Care-Seeking Advice, or Is It?

live_model.evidence: Methods: API calls via OpenRouter on April 23, 2025 for 'o3, gpt-4.1-nano, gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-4.1, gpt-4.5-preview, o4-mini and o4-mini-high'; Results: 'gpt-4.1-nano ... 44% (196/450)'

prompt.location: Methods, Case Vignettes / prompt paragraph (triage prompt quoted verbatim)

claim.judge: llm:gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 and gpt-4.1-mini (output classification) with manual adjudication

data.source: 45 validated case vignettes from prior studies (refs 24, 30); vignette text not printed in this paper

notes: OpenRouter API, not the chat UI; o4-mini (o4-mini-2025-04-16), o3-mini and gpt-4-turbo also evaluated (Table 1 agreement). Vignette availability is the soft gap.

resolution.plan: The 45 vignettes and their physician gold-standard triage levels come from the authors' earlier open-access vignette studies (ref. 24 Kopka et al. 2024 Sci Rep; ref. 30 Kopka & Feufel 2024 Front Digit Health), not from this paper. Take them from those publications, send the printed triage prompt plus vignette to gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 ten times each with a fresh context, map each answer to emergency/non-emergency/self-care (the paper used zero-shot gpt-4.1-nano/mini classification with manual adjudication of disagreements), and compute accuracy over 450; compare with 44% (196/450).
resolution.approximation: Vignette texts sourced from the cited papers' supplements; direct API instead of OpenRouter; manual adjudication replaced by a fixed classifier.
